description: Docs as Markdown in the repo: every concept drawn, the glossary as the vocabulary, links and diagrams that cannot quietly rot.

opinions.summary: Docs are Markdown in the repository, reviewed and versioned with the code they describe.
Every concept and process gets a diagram, followed by a sentence saying how to read it.
Each user-facing feature has a page that shows it, with a screenshot when the ui pack is installed.
A decision that shapes the project is recorded as an ADR, not buried in a chat or a commit.
Relative links and #anchors in Markdown point at a file and a heading that exist.
Image links point at files in the repository.
Every mermaid block is a well-formed diagram.
Terms the glossary says to avoid stay out of prose; code spans and fences are exempt.
A README opens with a purpose paragraph of at most two sentences under the H1.
README steps are at most 20 words, descriptive sentences at most 25, paragraphs at most 6 sentences.
README prose uses the active voice; a passive construction warns and never fails.
README prose holds no counts, dates, time-bound words or version numbers.
